statement: In the equation $4(2x - k) + 3 = 8x - 17$, $k$ is a constant. If the equation has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of $k$?

choices.misconception: I reached $-4k = -20$ but dropped the negative sign when dividing, so I got $k = -5$.
I moved the 3 to the right side by adding it, so I got $-4k = -17 + 3 = -14$ and $k = \dfrac{7}{2}$.
I ignored the $+3$ and matched $-4k$ with $-17$, so I got $k = \dfrac{17}{4}$.

hints: An equation has infinitely many solutions when both sides are the same expression for every $x$.
Expand the left side. The $x$ terms already match, so the constant terms must match too.
The left side is $8x - 4k + 3$. Set $-4k + 3 = -17$ and solve for $k$.

solutions.reliable: Expanding, the left side is $8x - 4k + 3$. Both sides have $8x$, so the equation is true for every $x$ exactly when the constants agree: $-4k + 3 = -17$. Then $-4k = -20$ and $k = 5$. Check: with $k = 5$ the left side is $8x - 20 + 3 = 8x - 17$, identical to the right side.
